result.label: Indicator - Arts and cultural activties
note:
[b]Arts and cultural activities[/b]

[b]How do we measure this?[/b]
Percentage of adults participating in arts and cultural activities.

[b]Source
[/b]Experience of culture, arts and heritage by adults in Northern Ireland, Department for Communities
[url=https://www.communities-ni.gov.uk/articles/culture-arts-and-heritage-statistics]Culture, arts and heritage statistics | Department for Communities[/url]

[b]Impact of Covid-19[/b]
Data collection for the 2024/25 CHS was carried out using a mix of telephone and face-to-face interviewing modes, a similar approach to that used in 2022/23 and 2023/24. For 2020/21 and 2021/22 data collection was by telephone interviewing due to the coronavirus (Covid-19) pandemic. There was also a reduction in the number of questions between 2020/21-2022/23. As a result, the figures from 2020/21 onwards are not directly comparable to previous years due to the significant changes to the survey in terms of methodology and content. While comparisons can be made for the years 2021/22 onwards, it is important to note that engagement in 2021/22 would have been impacted by closures due to Covid-19.

[b]Further information
[/b]1. Participation in arts and cultural activities is defined as the percentage of adults (aged 16+) who have done at least one of the following within the last 12 months; engaged in the arts, used the public library service, visited a museum or science centre or used PRONI services.
2. In 2019/20, the questions on visits to museums were revised and as a result figures for visits to museums for 2019/20 onwards are not comparable with previous years. Although this is one element of the overall culture and arts engagement rate, the impact of the change is lessened in the culture and arts estimates as the majority of those who visit museums also engage in some other way with culture and arts.
3. Following a move in 2020/21 from face-to-face interviewing to telephone interviewing to collect data, due to the coronavirus (Covid-19) pandemic, data collection for the Continuous Household Surveys 2021/22 to 2024/25 used a mix of telephone and face-to-face modes. 
4. Results from 2021/22 to 2024/25 are not directly comparable to previous years due to the significant changes to the survey in terms of methodology and content.
5. While comparisons can be made between 2021/22 and 2024/25, it is important to note that engaging in arts/cultural activities in 2021/22 would have been impacted by closures due to Covid-19.

[b]Deprivation[/b]
6. Figures above are based on the 2017 NIMDM. More information on the NI Multiple Deprivation Measures can be found here: [url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation[/url] 

[b]Urban Rural[/b]
7. All figures are defined according to the 2015 urban rural classification. More information on Urban Rural classifications can be found here: [url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/support/geography/urban-rural-classification]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/support/geography/urban-rural-classification[/url] 

[b]Religion[/b]
8. 'Other' includes those who stated a religion other than Catholic and Protestant and those who stated no religion.

[b]Disability[/b]
9. For this indicator, ‘disability’ is measured using ‘limiting long-standing illness’. Respondents are defined as having a limiting long standing illness if they have any physical or mental health conditions or illnesses lasting or expected to last for 12 months or more, and the condition(s) or illness(es) reduce their ability to carry out day to day activities.
10. Due to the changes to the survey mode and questionnaire as a result of the Covid-19 pandemic, disability was not included in the 2020/21 questionnaire.

[b]Dependants[/b]
11. For this indicator, 'has dependants' includes individuals who have responsibility for the care of: a child(ren); a person with a disability; and/or a dependant elderly person.
12. Data is provided from the first year available (2010/11).
